    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that at any given time, 16 million Americans are experiencing a crisis that requires urgent help from our legal system or government. The right assistance could transform their lives. But today, most never get it.

    In a recent development, atticus makes it easy for any sick or injured person in crisis to get the life-changing aid they deserve. In the last six years, we've become the leading platform connecting people with disabilities to government benefits. We’re also quickly scaling an injury practice to help victims of accidents, misconduct, and violence get compensation from insurance.

    According to recent reports, so far, we've helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10B in life-changing aid — and earned over 20,000+ five-star reviews. And we're just getting started.

    We've raised more than $100 million from top VC firms like Forerunner, GV (Google Ventures), and True Ventures, with ambitions to create a category defining business assisting Americans in need.

    Each month, tens of thousands of Americans seek our help for a single legal matter – applying for Social Security Disability, filing a Workers’ Compensation claim – but many of these clients are actually eligible for additional aid without ever knowing it.

    Your job as Lead Attorney, New Verticals is to help us do right by these clients, helping them claim additional benefits through the social safety net. You’ll oversee the team of intake specialists who speak with clients who have secondary claims, evaluating the case facts and whether to connect them with an Atticus attorney or local attorney to provide legal advice and potentially take on their case.

    According to recent reports, this is a job that straddles the line between practicing the law and growing a business. It requires developing a strong understanding of multiple fields of law, and being able to accurately identify when we can help and when we cannot. But even more importantly, this job requires you to be an incredibly strong operator: you need to keep the massive picture in mind and stay laser-focused on how we can achieve our goals, oftentimes finding outside-the-box ways to accomplish them. You will report to our General Manager of New Verticals and work closely with our CEO and Managing Attorney.

    On any given day, you’ll spend your time:.

    Speaking with severely injured clients trying to rebuild their lives after a catastrophic accident.

    Sourcing and vetting local counsel in individual markets, holding a high bar for representation quality and ending relationships that fall below it.

    Working with our data and insights team to identify existing clients who may have unrecognized claims in adjacent fields of law, and setting the standard for which ancillary cases we take on.

    Building the playbook for claim types we haven't handled before, starting by screening cases yourself and eventually creating the protocol our intake specialists will run at scale.

    This is a rare opportunity for an attorney to join a profitable and growing public-interest law firm and take on one of our biggest priorities as a company.

    You can understand the nuances of various contingency fields of law and can apply them to a variety of cases (including Social Security Disability, Workers’ Compensation, Personal Injury, and more) – you don’t need to be an expert today, but you should be a fast learner.

    You can empathize with anyone and quickly build rapport and relationships while exercising good judgment, both with our clients and local counsel at law firms across the country.

    You have strong instincts and judgment as an operator – you can run effective and efficient processes, and you don’t let them run you.

    You have a demonstrated commitment to doing good and helping people.

    You’ve built a track record as a great people manager – you know how to motivate talent and hold a high bar for output.

    You have meaningful work experience outside of serving as a lawyer, ideally at a startup or other fast-paced, agile environment (e.g., a business operations team).

    We are strongly committed to building a diverse team. If you're from a background that's underrepresented in tech, we'd love to meet you.

    This role offers a unique chance to join a startup that has strong traction (substantial funding, well-respected backers, tremendous growth, and many happy customers) but is still small enough that you can have a huge impact and play a role in shaping our success.

    According to recent reports, we're a certified B Corporation tackling a critical social problem. Our mission to help people in need drives everything we do, and your work here will touch many lives.

    We offer competitive pay — including equity — and generous benefits:.

    Medical and dental insurance with 100% of employees and their families premiums covered.

    15 vacation days & ~20 paid holidays each year (including two weeks at end-of-year).

    $1,000 reimbursable stipend for education and training outside of work.

    Up to $1,200/year student loan repayment assistance.

    401(k) match and optional HSA/FSA.

    Humble, thoughtful, smart, fun colleagues.

    According to recent reports, we anticipate the base salary band for this role will be between $140,000 and $175,000 in addition to equity and benefits. The salary at offer will be determined by a number of factors such as candidate's experience, knowledge, skills and abilities, as well as internal equity among our team.

    This job is fully remote and we’re committed to empowering everyone with flexibility. Work remotely, and travel to LA (on the company dime) as needed to be with your colleagues – usually quarterly, plus offsites. We care a lot about building a great culture and we think some interactions need to happen in person, so we put a lot of thought into retreats, offsites, and other ways to gather.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Pipelines team at Supabase. Supabase Pipelines is a managed change data capture product. It copies the tables you select from Supabase Postgres to other systems, then streams later changes. The product is in public alpha, with BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckLake and Snowflake destinations.

    Pipelines uses Postgres logical replication and Supabase ETL, our open source replication engine written in Rust. The team works close to the database. That means replication slots, WAL retention, initial table syncs, and the load they place on a customer's source database. The team also builds and runs the destination connectors. Correctness, ordering and recovery matter there as much as speed.

    • Industry observers note that so far, we’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10 billion in life-changing aid —and earned over 20,000 five-star reviews.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, at any given time, 16 million Americans are experiencing a crisis that requires urgent help from our legal system or government. The right assistance could transform their lives. But today, most never get it.

    Sources indicate that atticus makes it easy for any sick or injured American to get life-changing aid. Our mission is to tear down barriers between people in crisis and the aid they deserve. In the last six years, we’ve become the leading platform connecting people with disabilities to government benefits. We also help victims of accidents, misconduct, and violence get compensation from insurance.

    Industry observers note that so far, we’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10 billion in life-changing aid —and earned over 20,000 five-star reviews. And we’re just getting started.

    We've raised more than $100 million from top VC firms like Forerunner, Google Ventures, and True Ventures, and we’re on our way to creating a category defining business assisting Americans in need.

    Each day, thousands of people seek our help getting disability benefits or insurance compensation. They’re intimidated by the process, unsure where to turn, and desperate for good advice.

    It has been revealed that as a Legal Assistant at Atticus, your job is to ensure they get and stay on the right path. This job is different from that of a traditional legal assistant. The job mixes responsibilities in any good legal assistant’s comfort zone (build client relationships; support paralegals and attorneys in filing and managing claims) with those unique to being an operator in a fast-growing tech firm (help Marketing source clients who’d be great in testimonials, or user test upcoming tools for Product).

    In a typical week you might do any of the following:.

    Make contact with a client that’s in danger of slipping through the cracks at SSA, and help get their case back on track.

    Work with a client’s team to run down missing paperwork at SSA.

    Take on an inefficient workflow that’s slowing the team down (e.g., processing case updates), scope an improvement, get team buy-in, and execute the improvement.

    This role is a rare opportunity to join a fast-growing Series C startup and do meaningful social impact work. It’s designed to be a path to building expertise in the fields of law you support and taking on greater responsibilities over time (e.g. becoming a paralegal).

    You have a Bachelor’s degree from a four-year university with strong academic performance.

    You have experience in a professional role that required a substantial amount of customer-facing work and/or administrative tasks.

    You are a resourceful team-player ready to dive into a scrappy startup environment where you will learn rapidly and get your hands dirty.

    You are comfortable in a variety of interpersonal conversations; you can be empathetic and kind when speaking with people in a moment of crisis, and can be thoughtful and organized when interacting with attorneys or the SSA.

    You have a demonstrated commitment to doing good and helping people.

    You have professional experience helping others apply for government benefits.

    You have experience at a startup or other fast-paced, agile environment.

    Recent findings suggest that we are strongly committed to building a diverse team. If you’re from a background that’s underrepresented in tech, we’d love to meet you.

    This is a rare opportunity to join a startup that has strong traction (substantial funding, well-respected backers, tremendous growth, and many happy customers) but is still small enough that you can have a huge impact and play a role in shaping our culture.

    We’re a certified B Corporation tackling a critical social problem. Our mission to help people in need drives everything we do, and your work here will touch many lives.

    We offer competitive pay — including equity for every employee — and generous benefits:.

    Medical and dental insurance with 100% of employees and their families premiums covered.

    15 vacation days & ~20 paid holidays each year (including two weeks at the end-of-year).

    $1,000/year reimbursable stipend for education and training outside of work.

    Up to $1,200/year student loan repayment assistance.

    401(k) match and optional HSA/FSA.

    Humble, thoughtful, smart, fun colleagues.

    Recent findings suggest that we anticipate the base salary band for this role will be between $50,000 and $75,000 in addition to equity and benefits. The salary at offer will be determined by a number of factors such as candidate’s experience, knowledge, skills and abilities, as well as internal equity among our team.

    It has been revealed that this job is fully remote and we’re committed to empowering everyone with flexibility. Work remotely, and travel to LA (on the organization dime) as needed to be with your colleagues – usually quarterly, plus offsites. We care a lot about building a great culture and we think some interactions need to happen in person, so we put a lot of thought into retreats, offsites, and other ways to gather.

    • According to recent reports, kindred is revolutionizing the “third option” of travel accommodation, compared to short-term rentals and hotels.
    • To support that momentum, Kindred has raised over $150M in capital from some of the most credible investors in Silicon Valley, including Index Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, Latest Enterprise Associates, Bessemer Venture Partners, Caffeinated Capital, Elad Gil, and founders of companies like Opendoor, Figma, ClassPass, and more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that kindred is a members-only home swapping platform that unlocks the ability to live a travel-rich lifestyle through the power of community. By exchanging primary residences with trusted peers, renters and owners alike can match with Kindred spirits and explore new destinations without breaking the bank.

    According to recent reports, kindred is revolutionizing the “third option” of travel accommodation, compared to short-term rentals and hotels. Since launching in 2022, Kindred has grown to a global community of 300,000 members across 150+ cities and puts home swapping on the map as a radically more affordable, responsible, and connected way to travel.

    To support that momentum, Kindred has raised over $150M in capital from some of the most credible investors in Silicon Valley, including Index Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, Latest Enterprise Associates, Bessemer Venture Partners, Caffeinated Capital, Elad Gil, and founders of companies like Opendoor, Figma, ClassPass, and more.

    Kindred’s co-founders are proven leaders from the early team at Opendoor ($15B+ exit), who have each built and scaled products that today generate $1B+ annual revenue combined.

    We’re looking for the world’s top builders, executors, and believers to help us make travel more meaningful.

    You can learn more about us in Forbes and The Latest York Times.

    This is Kindred’s first dedicated public policy hire. You’ll join a three-person legal and policy team (reporting to the General Counsel) and own the execution of Kindred’s public policy and government relations efforts, with a focus on European markets but covering additional markets as necessary.

    Industry observers note that the role is primarily focused on proactive advocacy to shape the policy environment for home-swapping. You’ll build relationships with elected officials, regulators, and industry groups. You’ll commission and manage economic impact research. You’ll develop city-level partnerships that normalize home-swapping as a category distinct from other travel categories. You’ll also develop working familiarity with the tax, housing, and accommodation regulations that intersect with Kindred’s model, and help parse how those frameworks apply (or don’t) to credit-based home-swapping. You’ll do all of this initially as a team of one, with outside consultants to support you and a path to building a team as the firm grows and the function matures.

    Execute Kindred’s public policy strategy with an emphasis on proactive advocacy.

    Build and maintain relationships with elected officials, regulators, and staff at the local, state/provincial, and national levels. Represent Kindred in meetings, hearings, coalition convenings, and industry events.

    In a recent development, track proposed housing, short-term rental, tax, and platform regulations that could impact Kindred’s model, identifying where Kindred’s credit-based, non-commercial structure creates meaningful regulatory distinctions. Use AI-assisted tools and other technology to monitor developments across jurisdictions.

    Further develop and evolve Kindred’s core policy narrative and positioning materials. Draft position papers, comment letters, testimony, and advocacy materials.

    It has been revealed that propose and negotiate city-level partnerships that promote and normalize home-swapping. Build relationships with housing advocacy organizations, tourism boards, trade associations, and aligned industry coalitions.

    Commission and manage third-party economic analyses on the impact of Kindred’s model, collaborating with internal business teams and outside consulting firms.

    Identify, evaluate, and manage outside consultants cost-effectively (lobbyists, policy advisors, research firms).

    Partner with internal teams to develop externally facing materials and data packages for stakeholder engagements.

    Coordinate with the General Counsel on lobbying compliance, political activity disclosures, and regulatory filings.

    7–10 years of experience in public policy, with at least 3 years at a technology firm or similar fast paced environment.

    Experience building or meaningfully contributing to building a public policy or government relations function, not just operating within an established one.

    Track record of productive relationships with elected officials, regulators, and policy stakeholders.

    Experience managing outside consultants, lobbyists, or policy advisors across multiple jurisdictions.

    Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience drafting policy position papers, advocacy materials, or regulatory comments.

    Experience with policy matters in Europe, with an interest in policy work in upcoming jurisdictions.

    Fluency with AI tools and a willingness to integrate them into policy monitoring, research, and content development workflows.

    Willingness to operate as an individual contributor while building the function, with the judgment to know when to engage outside support.

    Experience in or adjacent to the sharing economy, home-sharing, travel, housing, or short-term rental sectors.

    Experience at a growth-stage firm (under 500 employees).

    Familiarity with vacation/short-term rental, housing, and land use regulations, as well as related tax regulations.

    Recent findings suggest that comfort with detailed regulatory analysis: ability to read and interpret statutes, ordinances, and administrative rules, and translate their implications into actionable policy positions. A law degree and legal practice experience is a plus but not required.

    Build something upcoming: You’ll help define the function and shape how Kindred engages with governments and regulators from the ground up.

    A genuinely different model: Kindred’s credit-based, non-commercial home-swapping model is structurally distinct from existing travel lodging categories, contributing to sustainable tourism objectives.

    Path to leadership: As the tech giant and function grow, this role offers the opportunity to greater leadership.

    Competitive compensation: Base plus meaningful equity in a growth-stage firm.

    According to recent reports, at Kindred, we know that good things happen when we look out for one another. We offer a thoughtful, human-first benefits package designed to support health, wellbeing, and connection.Our openings may span more than one career level. The base salary offered depends on factors such as experience, transferable skills, business needs, impact, and market data.

    Competitive cash compensation and equity.

    Private health insurance, pension contributions, and enhanced parental leave.

    25 days of annual leave, plus 8 paid bank holidays.

    21 credits per year to stay in Kindred homes.

    £3,200 annual travel stipend to help offset travel-related costs.

    Remote-first and remote-flexible, with a £400 annual budget to meet up with teammates and a yearly company-paid trip to Kindred HQ in San Francisco.

    Regular team and company offsites to connect, collaborate, and build together.

    A four-week paid sabbatical after five years with Kindred.

    A vibrant, inclusive, and highly skilled team that ferociously protects team chemistry.

    A culture of high standards, feedback, and continual growth.

    Kindred is committed to providing equal opportunities for all applicants and employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation, as protected by the Equality Act 2010, or on the basis of any other characteristic protected by law. If you need any adjustments during the application or interview process, please let us know.

    Senior Product Marketing Manager - Scaling Creators at Kit

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love.
    • Kit's most established creators run real companies, with teams, large lists, dedicated sending needs, and a buying process that our self-serve motion wasn't built to serve.
    • According to recent reports, you'll define who this buyer is, write the story that resonates and wins with them, and build the GTM strategy to drive inbound pipeline for our sales team.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

    Kit's most established creators run real companies, with teams, large lists, dedicated sending needs, and a buying process that our self-serve motion wasn't built to serve. Because this part of our business is growing, we're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Scaling Creators to own how Kit wins, lands, and expands these businesses through a sales-assisted motion that sits alongside our self-serve product.

    According to recent reports, you'll define who this buyer is, write the story that resonates and wins with them, and build the GTM strategy to drive inbound pipeline for our sales team. When these creators choose Kit and grow on it, they build more valuable businesses, and that's the outcome this role exists for.

    This is a full-time individual contributor role ideal for someone who has added an upmarket sales-led motion to a product-led company before and wants their work measured in win rate and deal size.

    You'll report to Christina Lhi, Head of Marketing, and work alongside two other experienced Product Marketing Managers on Kit's product marketing team. Together, you'll keep the self-serve and sales-assisted stories feeling like one Kit.

    You'll spend a lot of your time with:.

    Our sales leadership, on who we sell to, the deal toolkit, enablement, and win/loss.

    Account Executives and Solutions Consultants, on demo narratives, discovery, and technical and migration proof.

    Product, on packaging, launches, and roadmap input.

    RevOps and analytics, on how accounts get routed to sales, attribution, and pricing decisions.

    Creator Success, on case studies, customer references, and expansion plays.

    Demand gen, content, and events, on campaigns and events for established creators.

    Recent findings suggest that first Week: Dive into our onboarding curriculum in Notion and learn Kit's product, pricing, and current positioning. Attend Get-To-Know-You (GTKY) meetings with marketing, sales, Solutions Consultants, RevOps, and Creator Success. Get access to our CRM, call recordings, and product analytics, and start listening to recent sales calls. Understand how product marketing currently works at Kit.

    In a recent development, first Month: Shadow 15+ sales calls and talk with 10 established creators, including recent wins, losses, and churned accounts. Audit the sales content reps use today and how product usage currently routes accounts to sales. Set baselines with RevOps for win rate, sales cycle, deal size, and expansion revenue. Share a written point of view with the entire growth team on who our established creator buyer is and the three biggest gaps in how we sell to them. And an action plan on how we can win these creators.

    According to recent reports, first Year: Sales runs on messaging and tools you built, pitch with confidence and we drive 2X inbound MQLs from when you started. You’ll own and lead our channel strategy, setting the vision, driving cross-functional alignment, and partnering with Marketing to bring it to life. You'll run a quarterly win/loss program and share what you learn openly, build a clear path for sales leads on our website, and make sure introduces that matter to larger accounts ship with both a self-serve and a sales-assisted version. Your work has a direct impact on helping Kit reach $100,000,000 ARR while protecting the self-serve engine that got us here.

    Segmentation and buyer definition: turning firmographic and product usage data into a clear picture of who to sell to and when.

    Messaging and positioning for a sales-assisted buyer, including competitive differentiation and objection handling.

    Sales enablement that reps actually use: demo narratives, discovery guides, business cases, and battlecards.

    Writing and storytelling that turns product depth into a business case a non-technical buyer can act on.

    Working with CRM, product analytics, and pipeline data to measure funnel conversion, win rate, and deal size.

    Customer and market/competitor research, including win/loss interviews and call analysis.

    Systems thinking: connecting people, processes, data, and tools to identify opportunities and build repeatable solutions across the go-to-market motion.

    Strong AI fluency: knowing when to leverage AI and how to build AI-powered workflows or tools that scale product marketing work, with human judgment and quality checks built in.

    Pricing and packaging input for a newly introduced tier or add-on (nice to have).

    7+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, including at least 2 years supporting a sales team selling to mid-market and/or larger accounts.

    Added a sales-led motion on top of a product-led one at a high-growth organization, and can show what changed before and after with clear metrics.

    Built a deal toolkit and enablement program from little or nothing, and tied it to a sales metric like win rate or deal size.

    Ran a win/loss or customer research program that changed how a team sold or built.

    Ran an expansion or account-based program for an existing customer base (nice to have).

    Worked in email, martech, or the creator economy.

    You lead without a formal title. You align sales, product, RevOps, and finance on goals, trade-offs, and what success looks like, then keep things moving.

    You advocate for creators in decisions, and you protect the self-serve experience instead of pushing every account toward sales.

    You act with urgency and stay focused on hitting OKRs and owning outcomes.

    You work in public. You share findings, drafts, and the reasoning behind decisions so others can build on them.

    You connect data to decisions, and you help others get sharper about using it.

    You raise the bar on quality and iterate toward it, and you shape how your team uses AI, from call analysis to keeping battlecards current.

    According to recent reports, experience in only self-serve or only enterprise sales. This role lives in the space between them, and you'll need to understand both.

    Treating enablement as a deck handoff. The work includes coaching reps, measuring what gets used, and revising what doesn't land.

    Wanting a sales playbook already in place. Much of this motion doesn't exist yet, and you'll be building it as you learn.

    It has been revealed that preferring to be measured on output rather than outcomes. You'll share accountability with Sales for win rate, deal size, and expansion revenue.

    Industry observers note that needing extensive approval before acting. You'll be trusted to make calls on speed versus quality and to explain your reasoning.

    Discomfort with direct, candid feedback, especially from sellers on what's working in live deals.

    We're 100% remote with team members across the globe. We work mostly on East Coast time—so if you're based on the West Coast of the United States, Europe, or Asia, you might have a few early mornings or late evenings. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

    Kit has standardized salaries based on position, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re hiring at our level 4 ($166,000). Level is determined based on experience and our interview process.

    We cover up to $2,280 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance prepares through Aetna.

    $2,000 equipment allowance for your first two years, $1,000 budget every following two years. Manufacturer-provided laptops are issued to every Kit team member and are not included in the equipment budget.

    Individual learning + development budget ($3,500/year).

    Creator meetup budget ($50/month) to connect with creators over coffee, lunch, or other in-person meetups.

    Childcare benefit up to $3,000 annually through JOON.

    Twenty (20) days of paid time off during each year of employment.

    Paid paid vacation: An after-tax bonus of $1,000 for taking five consecutive days of vacation where you’re fully unplugged from work.

    Two weeks of paid sick time each year, including mental health + well being days.

    Twelve (12) weeks paid parental leave and flexible scheduling in your child’s first year.

    Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months.

    Industry observers note that winter Break Closure: Kit closes for a week at the end of December, giving everyone a collective break to enjoy the holiday season. Essential support services remain available, with teams coordinating to ensure coverage during this period.

    Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team.

    Fantastic in-person or virtual retreats with the team twice a year.

    According to recent reports, we usually receive a large number of applications, and our goal is to follow up with you within two weeks. You’ll hear from us either way. Here’s what you can expect from the rest of our hiring process:.

    A phone screen with our recruiter (30 min).

    Hiring manager interview (45 min).

    In a recent development, we’ll keep you informed through every step. To get started, complete this application, including a cover letter and answers to the questions on the next page. We read every single application, and your cover letter and responses help put your experience into context.

    Kit is an equal opportunity employer.

    It has been revealed that we value diversity in all of its forms. Research tells us that applicants who are female or non-binary, as well as applicants who are people of color, are less likely to apply for roles they do not feel 100% qualified for. If you think you meet more than 50% of our requirements but fewer than 100% of them, please apply.

    We’re imperfect communicators, so think of our job postings as the starting point for discussion rather than proof that you shouldn’t apply.

    Kit does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

    OpenAI Getting Rid of Custom GPTs and Moving to Plugin Architecture

    📅 05 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • OpenAI has declared it will retire Custom GPTs and move the specialized workflows built around them to a latest plugin architecture spanning ChatGPT and its Codex coding agent.
    • In a recent development, custom GPT retirement is currently scheduled for Dec.
    • It has been revealed that for affected Enterprise workspaces, OpenAI's current migration schedule targets Oct.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OpenAI has declared it will retire Custom GPTs and move the specialized workflows built around them to a latest plugin architecture spanning ChatGPT and its Codex coding agent.

    In a recent development, custom GPT retirement is currently scheduled for Dec. 11, 2026, although the organization notes timing and migration availability can vary by account and workspace.

    It has been revealed that for affected Enterprise workspaces, OpenAI's current migration schedule targets Oct. 26 for ending creation of upcoming Custom GPTs. Qualifying Enterprise customers with approved deferrals can continue using them until Feb. 11, 2027.

    OpenAI has changed its UI to make GPTs less prominent, and when users choose to try creating a new Custom GPT, they are now prompted with an option to create a plugin instead.

    Rather than maintaining separate customized versions of ChatGPT, OpenAI is shifting customization toward plugins that can package reusable instructions, reference material, and connections to outside services.

    In a recent development, under OpenAI's plugin architecture, a plugin can include one or more skills containing instructions and resources for repeatable workflows, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing tools and external systems, or both. ChatGPT and Codex share a universal plugin directory, although some capabilities can remain specific to a particular environment.

    For organizations, that makes the change more than a simple renaming exercise. A company could package recurring workflows into skills while using MCP servers or connected apps to give those workflows access to enterprise systems and data.

    OpenAI notes creators will be able to migrate an existing GPT through the My GPTs interface. The GPT's instructions become a skill in the replacement plugin, while knowledge files are copied into plugin reference files and connected apps can be carried over.

    Not everything transfers automatically. Existing GPT conversations do not migrate, the selected model does not carry over, and Custom Actions may have to be rebuilt using an available app or a custom MCP server.

    Sources indicate that sharing also changes. Migrated plugins start private, existing GPT consumers do not automatically receive access to the replacement, and prior sharing settings do not carry over.

    In a recent development, openAI is also cautioning organizations against assuming that migration will preserve behavior exactly. "A migrated plugin may respond differently," the manufacturer states, recommending that users retest familiar prompts, reference-material use, required output formats, and integrations before relying on the replacement.

    That warning has contributed to pushback from some GPT builders, who argue that plugins do not fully reproduce the dedicated and predictable environment of a Custom GPT. Other complaints have focused on sharing, migration complexity, and differences in how migrated workflows use instructions and reference material.

    Recent findings suggest that despite those concerns, OpenAI is clearly consolidating around plugins as its common mechanism for extending its AI products. Its developer documentation now describes plugins as packages people can "discover, install, share, and publish" across ChatGPT and Codex, replacing the separate-custom-assistant model with reusable AI capabilities that can be combined with enterprise tools and services.

    For more information, go to the OpenAI site.

    David Ramel is an editor and writer at Converge 360.

    Anthropic confirmed it is introducing machine-readable watermarks to text generated by supported Claude models as it moves to comply with European Union AI transparency rules.

    Unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity organization Sophos.

    AI agents have moved into mainstream enterprise use, but the content infrastructure needed to support them has struggled to keep up, according to a upcoming report from cloud content management firm Box.

    Microsoft has published a draft code of conduct that lays out how its homegrown AI models should behave, with human control taking priority over model capability, autonomy, and even task completion.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Enterprise ambitions around AI are running into a fundamental problem: Orgnanizations aren't always confident in the networks those projects depend on, according to a report from telecommunications provider Arelion.
    • The research found that concerns about network providers have caused organizations to rethink strategic initiatives over the past two years.
    • The findings come from Arelion's report, "The Trust Illusion: Why AI and Digital Transformation Need More Than a Reliable Network," based on a survey of 518 senior enterprise network decision-makers in the U.S., U.K., Germany, and France conducted by Savanta.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise ambitions around AI are running into a fundamental problem: Orgnanizations aren't always confident in the networks those projects depend on, according to a report from telecommunications provider Arelion.

    The research found that concerns about network providers have caused organizations to rethink strategic initiatives over the past two years. Among respondents whose initiatives were affected, AI and data-driven projects were the most cited, at 49%. That put AI ahead of security and compliance programs at 44%, digital transformation at 42%, and cloud migration at 38%.

    The findings come from Arelion's report, "The Trust Illusion: Why AI and Digital Transformation Need More Than a Reliable Network," based on a survey of 518 senior enterprise network decision-makers in the U.S., U.K., Germany, and France conducted by Savanta.

    All respondents worked for organizations with more than 2,000 employees and influenced network strategy across data centers, cloud, and connectivity. Of those surveyed, 66% had final sign-off responsibility. The results suggest that as organizations pursue increasingly data-intensive AI projects, confidence in the network infrastructure supporting them could become another deployment obstacle.

    On the surface, Arelion found little evidence of a trust crisis. A total of 93% of respondents remarked they largely or completely trust their current network provider, while 83% said that trust has strengthened over time.

    The picture changes when respondents are asked about a serious network incident. Only 15% stated they have complete confidence in their provider's ability to promptly detect and address such a problem. Another 42% said their provider seriously lets them down anywhere from a few times a year to monthly or more frequently.

    Those concerns have consequences beyond the network itself. Responding organizations have delayed, scaled back, or stopped strategic initiatives because of provider trust concerns, while others have added resiliency or risk-mitigation measures.

    AI and data projects were the most affected among respondents reporting an impact, as organizations try to move AI from experimentation into larger production deployments.

    It has been revealed that A serious provider failure could also have substantial consequences. Forty percent of respondents noted such an event would cause major operational disruption, while 18% anticipated significant financial loss or severe financial or reputational damage.

    Sources indicate that another tension runs through Arelion's findings. Enterprises need networks they can trust to support AI projects, but many of the same decision-makers are concerned about AI's growing role inside those networks. A total of 54% of respondents identified AI and automation in network management and security as the factors most likely to negatively affect network trust over the next three years. That ranked ahead of data sovereignty expectations and geopolitical instability, both at 39%, and regulatory requirements and quantum computing threats to current encryption standards, both at 38%.

    At the same time, respondents aren't rejecting AI as a network technology. Proactive AI-driven fault prediction was among the capabilities they remarked would matter most to future trust, alongside stronger built-in security, greater accountability, and responsive support. That leaves enterprises in an unusual position: AI is increasing their dependence on digital infrastructure while also raising questions about how that infrastructure itself is managed.

    Arelion has an interest in emphasizing the importance of network-provider trust, and the survey reflects the views specifically of network decision-makers at large enterprises. Still, the findings point to an infrastructure consideration that can get lost amid the rush to adopt new AI models and agents. AI projects ultimately depend on the networks, cloud environments, data centers, and connectivity beneath them. If organizations lack confidence in that foundation, access to better AI models alone won't remove the obstacle.

    It has been revealed that "Trust is influencing which strategic initiatives move forward, how organizations manage risk, and which providers they choose to work with," noted Mattias Fridström, Vice President at Arelion. "As businesses become increasingly reliant on digital infrastructure, enterprises are looking for network providers that can demonstrate transparency, accountability, and operational excellence, not just availability.".

    The full report is available for download here at the Arelion site (registration required).

    • Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research Digital Realty.
    • The Global Data Insights Survey 2026 points to a widening mix of infrastructure models behind enterprise AI.
    • The research is based on an online survey of 2,131 IT decision-makers across 19 countries, and 11 industries, conducted from Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Enterprise AI projects are running into infrastructure questions as organizations move from planning toward deployment, according to recent research Digital Realty. Forty percent of survey respondents cited a lack of specialized infrastructure required by AI as a main challenge to adopting a formal AI strategy, up from 9% in the manufacturer's 2024 research.

    The Global Data Insights Survey 2026 points to a widening mix of infrastructure models behind enterprise AI. Half of respondents host AI models in private clouds, 86% are pursuing or exploring sovereign AI, 92% tie data-location strategy to their AI plans, and 88% follow a distributed-data approach.

    The research is based on an online survey of 2,131 IT decision-makers across 19 countries, and 11 industries, conducted from Nov. 23, 2025, through Feb. 4, 2026.

    Industry observers note that organizations also appear to be shifting from AI planning toward execution. The share actively executing AI to achieve operational efficiency or reduce costs rose from 27% in 2024 to 37% this year. Only 3% reported no measurable ROI to date, while 63% expect returns within the next six months to two years.

    In a recent development, specialized infrastructure led the survey's list of AI adoption challenges at 40%, followed by regulatory and personal-data concerns at 35%. Data availability and quality, storage capacity, interconnection, compute resources, and staffing also ranked as significant constraints.

    Those requirements are also shaping workload placement. Integration with existing IT or data infrastructure ranked first at 43%, while regulatory compliance and performance were each cited by 37%. Data proximity, sovereignty, sustainability, cost, and intellectual property protection also factored into hosting decisions.

    Recent findings suggest that private cloud features prominently across the report's AI hosting categories, but enterprises are clearly using a mix of private cloud, public cloud, on-premises infrastructure, and colocation. Private cloud accounted for 50% of custom-built AI model hosting and 47% for open source or fine-tuned large language models (LLMs).

    It has been revealed that sovereignty is another part of that placement decision. Thirty-two percent consider sovereign AI — in which data and AI models remain within a single national or regulatory jurisdiction — a requirement, while another 54% are exploring it. The findings point toward hybrid environments in which infrastructure location, governance and data control increasingly overlap.

    #20474. Tech Report: OpenAI Intros Dots, AI Agents that Continue Working Between User Conversations

    📅 07 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (697 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: OpenAI Intros Dots, AI Agents that Continue Working Between User Conversations

    📅 07 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (697 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • OpenAI has introduced Dots, GPT-6 Astra-powered agents that run on their own cloud computers, using connected applications to carry on with assignments between conversations and incorporating people' feedback as they go.
    • It has been revealed that openAI is also previewing specialist Dots for organizations, with separate identities and credentials for defined responsibilities.
    • The broader ambition seems to be to make delegation last beyond a chat session.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OpenAI has introduced Dots, GPT-6 Astra-powered agents that run on their own cloud computers, using connected applications to carry on with assignments between conversations and incorporating people' feedback as they go.

    It has been revealed that openAI is also previewing specialist Dots for organizations, with separate identities and credentials for defined responsibilities. Those enterprise deployments are beginning with focused pilots. The tech giant is working with Microsoft on integration with Agent 365's governance and security controls.

    The broader ambition seems to be to make delegation last beyond a chat session. That change could reduce the need to repeatedly explain a project. It also makes supervision a continuing obligation: An instruction that was appropriate yesterday may no longer fit today's circumstances.

    One notable distinction appears in OpenAI's privacy and safety FAQ. Disconnecting an application stops newly introduced access through that connection, but does not delete information already incorporated into a Dot's context.

    In a recent development, users currently cannot inspect or directly edit individual Dot memories. Deleting a Dot deletes its own context, while files and conversations it created remain separately stored. Plugin permissions are shared across Dots, ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex.

    In a recent development, for an organization, that creates two related governance questions: what an agent can retrieve now, and what it already knows. Revoking a connection addresses the first without necessarily resolving the second.

    OpenAI's safety account distinguishes authorized tasks that continue in the background from unsolicited "proactive research." The latter uses tools restricted to reading permitted sources. Those research tasks cannot directly send messages, change connected application content, or control a browser or desktop. Any subsequent action must pass the usual rules and checks.

    A separate system, Auto-review, checks certain planned actions against instructions and safety requirements. OpenAI notes the agent cannot modify the controls enforcing those checks.

    "Dots can still make mistakes," the manufacturer cautions.

    In a recent development, openAI's Dots system-card appendix acknowledges that persistence and multi-agent systems are not new. Its evaluations examine how continuing work affects authorization boundaries.

    In one test involving successive related tasks, moderate scope violations increased from 8.6% to 19.7% when the number of intervening tasks doubled from five to 10. Examples included carrying information between unrelated tasks or editing a shared document beyond the intended scope. The tech giant reported no severe breaches or exfiltration in that evaluation.

    These are controlled test results, not measured failure rates in customer deployments. They nevertheless identify a problem that a successful demonstration cannot settle: whether an agent keeps the right boundaries as its workload accumulates.

    According to OpenAI's DevDay recap, Dots are available to Pro and Business Premium people in eligible markets. Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare access is an administrator-enabled beta, off by default.

    Sources indicate that the operational question is how organizations will keep delegated authority current. A continuing assignment needs a human owner who can revise its scope and decide when to stop it. Otherwise, the convenience of leaving work with an agent can outlast the reason it was authorized.

    For more information, go to the OpenAI site.

    Existing relationships with tier one financial and crypto media.

    Comfort using AI tools to automate data pulls and drafts.

    Mandarin, given our close work with Chinese speaking partners and media.

    #20463. Survey Identifies Data Governance Enforcement Gap for Agentic AI Tools

    📅 07 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (800 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Survey Identifies Data Governance Enforcement Gap for Agentic AI Tools

    📅 07 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to a new survey from identity security company Delinea, 99.7% of IT and security leaders said their organization has a formal policy governing what data AI tools and agents are permitted to access.
    • That disconnect is at the center of Delinea's fall 2026 Identity Security Report, "The AI Enforcement Gap," which suggests companies have made quick progress establishing AI governance but have not necessarily built the technical controls needed to enforce it.
    • The findings come from a pair of surveys covering 2,254 IT and security leaders and 2,250 non-IT employees at organizations with at least 500 employees across the U.S, U.K, Germany, Australia, Singapore, UAE, France, and India.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to a new survey from identity security company Delinea, 99.7% of IT and security leaders said their organization has a formal policy governing what data AI tools and agents are permitted to access. Yet only about 51% said AI access is checked against those policies in real time. Perhaps more worrying is that only 19% said their organization could detect in real time when an agent last accessed data outside its intended scope.

    That disconnect is at the center of Delinea's fall 2026 Identity Security Report, "The AI Enforcement Gap," which suggests companies have made quick progress establishing AI governance but have not necessarily built the technical controls needed to enforce it.

    The findings come from a pair of surveys covering 2,254 IT and security leaders and 2,250 non-IT employees at organizations with at least 500 employees across the U.S, U.K, Germany, Australia, Singapore, UAE, France, and India.

    All the organizations were using or piloting AI, while the employees surveyed used at least one AI tool for work.

    The problem becomes more consequential as companies move from AI tools that primarily respond to people toward agents capable of taking actions on their behalf.

    Eighty-seven percent of IT and security respondents remarked their organization had experienced or suspected of an incident during the past year in which an AI tool or agent accessed sensitive information beyond what was required for its task.

    Delinea's research also suggests companies are giving agents access that can persist longer than necessary. Only 58% of IT and security leaders said they have mechanisms that automatically revoke or expire AI access when a session ends, and those controls do not necessarily cover every agent or tool. Forty-two percent said many agent credentials remain active until an audit.

    Sources indicate that agents also are not always receiving their own narrowly defined permissions. Half of IT leaders noted their organizations use the employee's existing permissions as a boundary for what an agent can access. That can effectively hand an agent years of accumulated access belonging to the person who released it.

    In a recent development, that is particularly significant because an AI agent does not necessarily behave like a traditional service account. A service account typically performs a predefined process, while an agent can choose different tools, actions and sequences at runtime depending on the situation.

    "Service accounts run fixed scripts," said Mike Albrecht, associate director in the Risk Advisory Practice at Cross Country Consulting. "An AI agent decides what actions it's going to take at runtime.".

    The enforcement problem is not limited to autonomous agents.

    According to recent reports, the researchers found that 76% of employees surveyed had bypassed formal approval at some point to use AI tools with firm data, applications or systems. And 48% noted they always or extensively use AI tools without going through formal approval.

    Meanwhile, 60% remarked they had felt pressure to use AI with sensitive or confidential information even when they were not sure doing so was permitted.

    Executives were particularly likely to circumvent the process. Eighty-one percent of C-level respondents said they always or regularly bypass AI access approval, compared with 33% of intermediate-level employees.

    Industry observers note that the result is a widening gap between written AI governance and what companies can see and control. Delinea found that only 41% of IT leaders stated all AI tools and agents accessing company data are actively monitored. When an AI tool or agent went outside its intended scope, 55% said it took at least a day to detect the incident, while 30% said detection took four days or longer.

    That suggests the next phase of enterprise AI governance may depend less on writing additional rules and more on whether organizations can enforce existing ones while an agent is working.

    In a recent development, "Most organizations cannot confidently answer three questions: What agents are running in our environment? What can they access? What have they actually done?" remarked Delinea CEO Art Gilliland. "An agent can begin a session with legitimate access and drift into something it was never meant to do.".

    The full report is available for download here.

    Microsoft has published a draft code of conduct that lays out how its homegrown AI models should behave, with human control taking priority over model capability, autonomy, and even task completion.
